summary: A provisional new entry is warranted by locative sakən in 24/200. Stem I and Part act. are cautious filing choices for a borrowed predicate, not a demonstrated finite Turoyo paradigm. Preterit and Infectum are unattested.

Direct restricted lookups entry skn, form sakən and form Sakini returned no skn entry; loose šky/šny matches do not establish identity. No external dictionary was opened; the Ritter identifications are reader reports in the supplied input.

In 24/200 sakən has a plural compound subject a greʕayḏe w i aṯto but no overt plural marking, whereas coordinated ʕamire is plural. This favors a possibly invariant loan predicate over an inferred agreement paradigm.
JTM 3.2/34 coordinates sakən with baḥ ḥaye and is translated wohlauf und am Leben. Residence versus a general continuing state cannot be isolated securely; no wellbeing sense is added.
JTM 3.3/7 Sakini is excluded from the verbal evidence because the reported alternative nonverbal sakini dauernd remains viable. Its apparent -i must not be used to construct a plural paradigm.

Does JTM 3.2/34 sakən mean residing, settled, quiet or well? The supplied translation alone cannot resolve it.
